newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end up on short covering, buy stops.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end up on short covering, buy stops.

text.p: CME lean hog futures rallied to closing gains on short covering and buy stops while pork belly futures closed lower with nearbys pressured by weak cash belly prices, traders said.
Hog futures closed unchanged to 0.800 cent per lb higher with August up most at 80.650 cents. Pork bellies finished 1.000 lower to 0.700 higher with August off most at 77.500.

Hog futures had retreated from early gains as demand lacked follow through but the market rallied as selling also lacked follow through and floor talk on cash hogs turned steady to pssibly firm, traders said.

Early cash hog indications for Thursday were lower but reports that some packers need hogs and continued lighter-than-expected marketings turned cash ideas steadier. Some forecasts for warmer weather to return to the Midwest by the weekend also lent support after sparking the initial run up in values, they said.
Strength in futures came despite the continued weak tone to cash pork products. Back months showed support most of the day on firm technicals, they added.

Rand Financials and R.J. O'Brien bought August late. Refco was also doing the "Goldman roll" along with Cargill Investor Services, rolling long August positions by the Goldman Sachs commodity index fund into October, pit sources said.

In hog options, R.J. O'Brien sold December 76 and 78 calls while ADM Investor Services sold August 77/84 straddle. Volatility was down in July on the time decay while unchanged in other months, pit sources added.
Nearby pork belly futures were pressured late by further declines in cash bellies before local short covering pared losses in the closing range, traders said.

Heavy-weight, 16-18 lb cash bellies traded down another $1 per cwt to $80 and other weights ranged down to $79 in USDA's carlot pork report at midday. Heavy-weight belly prices have fallen $10 in the past week and were down to lowest levels since June 25.
Hammer Trading, R.J. O'Brien, Rand Financials and LFG notably sold August early, pit sources said.
